function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (`nvidia-a6000`) |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM) – you can change this to suit your workload |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (pick any zone that supports GPUs) |
| **Project** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` – replace with your actual GCP project ID |
| **Instance name** | `rtx-a6000-ubuntu20` |

---

## 1.  Prerequisites

1. **Enable the Compute Engine API**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Create a service account** (or use your user credentials) and download a JSON key.  
   ```bash
   gcloud iam service-accounts create rtx-a6000-sa \
       --display-name="RTX A6000 Service Account"

   gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
       --member="serviceAccount:rtx-a6000-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
       --role="roles/compute.admin"

   gcloud iam service-accounts keys create ~/rtx-a6000-key.json \
       --iam-account=rtx-a6000-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com
   ```

3. **Authenticate** (if using the CLI)  
   ```bash
   gcloud auth activate-service-account rtx-a6000-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
       --key-file=~/rtx-a6000-key.json
   ```

---

## 2.  Create the Instance with the **gcloud CLI**

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=./startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

> **Notes**  
> * `--metadata-from-file startup-script=./startup.sh` is optional – you can supply a script that installs CUDA, cuDNN, etc.  
> * `--tags` are optional but useful if you want to open ports (e.g., 22 for SSH, 80/443 for web).  
> * `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` ensures the VM can be live‑migrated during maintenance.

---

## 3.  Create the Instance with the **REST API**

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a custom application), use the following POST request.

### 3.1  Endpoint

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
```

### 3.2  Request Body (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20",
  "machineType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### 3.3  Authentication

* Use OAuth 2.0 with a **Bearer token** that has the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope.  
* Example using `curl` (replace `ACCESS_TOKEN`):

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

---

## 4.  Verify the Instance

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=us-central1-a
```

Look for:

* `accelerators` → should list `nvidia-a6000`
* `status` → `RUNNING`
* `networkInterfaces` → external IP

---

## 5.  Optional: Install CUDA & cuDNN

If you used the `startup-script` metadata, the instance will automatically install CUDA.  
Otherwise, SSH into the VM and run:

```bash
# Update & install prerequisites
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential dkms

# Add NVIDIA package repositories
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
sudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb
sudo cp /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg /usr/share/keyrings/
sudo apt-get update

# Install CUDA
sudo apt-get -y install cuda

# Install cuDNN (example for cuDNN 8.9)
# Download cuDNN tarball from NVIDIA Developer site, then:
tar -xzvf cudnn-linux-x86_64-8.9.5.28_cuda12-archive.tar.xz
sudo cp -P cuda/include/cudnn*.h /usr/local/cuda/include
sudo cp -P cuda/lib64/libcudnn* /usr/local/cuda/lib64
sudo chmod a+r /usr/local/cuda/include/cudnn*.h /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudnn*
```

---

### TL;DR

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1`
* **REST**: POST to `/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with `accelerators` field set to `nvidia-a6000`.

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `us-central1-a`, and any other placeholders with your own values. Happy GPU computing!
